title: The Riemann Sphere and Möbius Transformations

items.title: The Riemann sphere is the published one-point compactification of the complex plane
items.strategy: Cite the existing one-point compactification item and fix the notation \(\widehat{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}\) for the rest of the page.

items.title: The standard holomorphic charts on the Riemann sphere, with holomorphy and poles at infinity
Stereographic projection identifies the Riemann sphere with the unit two-sphere
items.strategy: Write the projection and its inverse explicitly, check continuity in coordinates, and then use compact-to-Hausdorff homeomorphism to finish.

items.title: The chordal metric on the Riemann sphere
The chordal metric induces the standard topology of the Riemann sphere
items.strategy: Transport the Euclidean metric of the unit sphere through stereographic projection and compare the resulting neighborhoods with the one-point-compactification topology.

items.title: Meromorphic functions on the Riemann sphere
Möbius transformations of the Riemann sphere
The cross-ratio of an ordered quadruple of sphere points
Circlines and their reflections on the Riemann sphere
Möbius transformations form a group and identify with the projective linear quotient of GL_2(C)
items.strategy: Compose fractional linear maps by matrix multiplication, identify scalar matrices as the kernel, and use the quotient vocabulary already developed earlier in the library.

items.title: Every Möbius transformation is a biholomorphism of the Riemann sphere
items.strategy: Check the chart formulas away from the pole and at infinity, then write the inverse map by the inverse matrix.

items.title: A unique Möbius transformation carries any ordered triple of distinct sphere points to any other
items.strategy: Write the normalizing map to \(0,1,\infty\) by a cross-ratio formula and compose the two normalizations.

items.title: The cross-ratio is invariant under Möbius transformations
items.strategy: Reduce to the unique normalizing map that sends three of the points to \(0,1,\infty\), then compute the fourth coordinate there.

items.title: Four distinct sphere points lie on one circline exactly when their cross-ratio is real
items.strategy: Move three points to \(0,1,\infty\), where circlines become the real line or a circle through infinity, and read the condition off directly.

items.title: Möbius transformations preserve circlines and conjugate their reflections
items.strategy: Transport a circline to the real line by three-point transitivity, compute the standard reflection there, and conjugate back.

items.title: Meromorphic functions on the Riemann sphere are exactly the rational functions
items.strategy: Compactness gives finitely many poles, subtract their principal parts, and apply Liouville to the resulting entire function on the finite chart.

items.title: The degree of a rational self-map of the Riemann sphere
A nonconstant rational map has total fibre multiplicity equal to its degree
items.strategy: Apply the argument principle to \(R(z)-w\) after sending infinity to a regular chart and read the total zero multiplicity from the pole order at infinity.

items.title: Every biholomorphic self-map of the Riemann sphere is Möbius
items.strategy: A sphere automorphism is meromorphic, hence rational; bijectivity forces degree one, and degree-one rational maps are exactly Möbius transformations.

items.title: Every biholomorphic self-map of the complex plane is affine
items.strategy: Extend the map across infinity as a sphere automorphism and then read off the condition that infinity stays fixed.

items.title: Every biholomorphic self-map of the punctured plane is of the form az or a/z
items.strategy: Extend across the missing points as a sphere automorphism and observe that a punctured-plane automorphism preserves the set \(\{0,\infty\}\).

items.title: Nonidentity Möbius transformations are parabolic or conjugate to a dilation, with the projective trace invariant
items.strategy: Classify by the number of fixed points, normalize those fixed points to \(\infty\) or \(0,\infty\), and record the projectively well-defined trace-squared-over-determinant invariant.

title: The Riemann Sphere and Möbius Transformations — Examples

items.title: The Cayley transform carries the upper half-plane biholomorphically onto the unit disc
items.strategy: Check directly that \((z-i)/(z+i)\) sends the real axis to the unit circle and the upper half-plane to its interior, then invert the formula.

items.title: A Möbius transformation is recovered from three point correspondences
items.strategy: Normalize both triples to \(0,1,\infty\) and compose the two normalizing maps.

items.title: The maps z+1, 2z, and 1/z realize the parabolic, hyperbolic, and elliptic branches of the classification
items.strategy: Compute fixed points and conjugacy normal forms directly from the defining formulas.

items.title: Stereographic projection and its inverse are explicit in coordinates
items.strategy: Evaluate the formulas in both directions and check the north-pole and infinity conventions directly.

items.title: The chordal distance has the standard coordinate formula on the finite plane
items.strategy: Transport two finite points to the sphere, compute the Euclidean distance there, and simplify the expression algebraically.

items.title: The exponential function is meromorphic on C but not meromorphic on the Riemann sphere
items.strategy: Its singularity at infinity is essential, so the rational-function theorem excludes it from sphere-meromorphicity.

items.title: The exponential map is a holomorphic surjection C to C^× that is not an automorphism
items.strategy: Use periodicity to show noninjectivity while the punctured-plane automorphism theorem records the genuine automorphisms.

items.title: Complex conjugation is a homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere that is not holomorphic
items.strategy: It preserves the underlying sphere topology but reverses orientation and cannot be a Möbius transformation.

items.title: FALSE: every Möbius self-map of the Riemann sphere restricts to an entire biholomorphism of the complex plane
items.strategy: A genuine pole on the finite plane blocks restriction to an entire bijection, so only the affine branch survives.

items.title: FALSE: a Möbius transformation with three fixed points can be nonidentity
items.strategy: Uniqueness on ordered triples forces any Möbius map fixing three distinct sphere points to be the identity.

items.title: FALSE: every self-homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere preserves the cross-ratio
items.strategy: Complex conjugation preserves the sphere topologically but changes nonreal cross-ratios by conjugation.

items.title: FALSE: the Riemann sphere is homeomorphic to the complex plane
items.strategy: The sphere is compact while the complex plane is not, so no homeomorphism can exist.

items.title: Every plane domain has the canonical nested compact exhaustion by distance and radius cutoffs
items.strategy: Use Euclidean closedness and boundedness for each stage, then check interior nesting and exhaustion directly from the distance-to-boundary definition.

items.title: Locally uniform convergence on a plane domain is the already-published compact-convergence notion
items.strategy: Cite the published dictionary and fix the local notation for this page's function spaces.

items.title: The exhaustion metric on a function space over a plane domain
The exhaustion metric induces exactly the topology of locally uniform convergence
items.strategy: Compare metric tails with sup bounds on finitely many exhaustion members and use the local-uniform dictionary in both directions.

items.title: The compact-open topology on C(Ω,C) is independent of the chosen compact exhaustion
items.strategy: Different exhaustion metrics induce the same locally uniform topology, and that topology is the compact-open topology on a metric domain.

items.title: Continuous complex-valued functions on a plane domain are complete for an exhaustion metric
items.strategy: A Cauchy sequence is uniformly Cauchy on each exhaustion member, so the local limits glue to a continuous function and the weighted metric forces convergence back to it.

items.title: Holomorphic functions form a closed subspace for locally uniform convergence
items.strategy: Apply the Weierstrass convergence theorem inside the complete continuous-function space.

items.title: Normal families of holomorphic functions on a plane domain
Locally bounded families of functions on a plane domain
Locally equicontinuous families of functions on a plane domain
Locally bounded holomorphic families are locally equicontinuous
items.strategy: Use a slightly larger disc and Cauchy's formula to convert one common bound into a uniform Lipschitz estimate on the smaller disc.

items.title: Montel's theorem: every locally bounded holomorphic family is normal
items.strategy: On each exhaustion member, local boundedness gives equicontinuity; then compact-domain Ascoli provides successive compact convergence, and a diagonal extraction gives the global subsequence.

items.title: Normal holomorphic families are locally bounded
items.strategy: If one compact neighborhood carried arbitrarily large values, choose a sequence and evaluation points there; compactness of the neighborhood and local uniform convergence of a normal subsequence contradict boundedness of its limit.

items.title: Vitali-Porter convergence theorem for holomorphic functions
items.strategy: Montel gives a locally uniformly convergent subsequence, and the identity theorem forces any two subsequential limits agreeing on a set with an interior limit point to coincide.

items.title: Every derivative operator is continuous for locally uniform convergence on holomorphic functions
items.strategy: Apply the already-published Weierstrass convergence theorem and restate its derivative conclusion as continuity of the derivative maps.

items.title: Chordal local uniform convergence and meromorphic normality
A chordally locally uniform meromorphic limit is meromorphic or identically infinity
items.strategy: Work in a sphere chart away from the limiting poles, use local compact convergence there, and invoke Hurwitz to control the branch where the limit takes the value infinity.

items.title: Local chordal equicontinuity is equivalent to meromorphic normality on compact exhaustions
items.strategy: Apply compact-metric Ascoli on each exhaustion member with the chordal sphere as target, then combine the compact convergence theorem with a diagonal extraction.

title: Normal Families and Montel's Theorem — Examples

items.title: The family z^n is normal on the unit disc and not normal on the complex plane
items.strategy: Bound the family on compacta of the disc and apply Montel there, then use local boundedness failure on large circles in the plane.

items.title: The family of holomorphic functions bounded by one is normal on every plane domain
items.strategy: Uniform bound one on every compact subset is exactly the hypothesis of Montel.

items.title: Montel's diagonal extraction can be written out concretely on a disc
items.strategy: Take successive subsequences on the compact discs of radius 1-1/n and follow the diagonal subsequence.

items.title: The exhaustion metric is explicit on the unit disc
items.strategy: Use the canonical compact exhaustion of the disc and write the first few weighted sup terms directly.

items.title: The family nz is not normal on any domain containing zero
items.strategy: The family is not locally bounded near the origin, so the converse-to-Montel theorem excludes normality.

items.title: The family e^(nz) converges chordally to infinity on the right half-plane without being holomorphically normal there
items.strategy: Real parts tend to plus infinity on compacta of the right half-plane, so the reciprocal tends uniformly to zero while the finite-valued holomorphic limit does not exist.

items.title: FALSE: a normal family contains every locally uniform sequential limit of its own sequences
items.strategy: Normality guarantees subsequential convergence, not closure of the family under limits.

items.title: FALSE: Arzelà-Ascoli alone proves Montel's theorem
items.strategy: The real work is the holomorphic equicontinuity step; without it the compactness theorem has no hypothesis to apply.

items.title: FALSE: a chordally locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions can never be identically infinity
items.strategy: The right-half-plane exponential family gives the standard contrary witness.
